title: Chicken Satay with Peanut Sauce
description: Chicken Satay is a classic Thai street food featuring tender marinated chicken skewers grilled over high heat and served with a rich, creamy peanut sauce. Balanced with sweet, savory, tangy, and smoky flavors, it is perfect as an appetizer or main course.

ingredients.title: For the Chicken Satay
items: 600g (1.3 lbs) boneless, skinless chicken thighs (preferred for juiciness)
2 tsp palm sugar (or light brown sugar)
1 tsp curry powder (yellow Thai or Madras)
1 tbsp lemongrass, finely minced (white tender part only)

ingredients.title: For the Peanut Sauce
items: 4 tbsp roasted unsalted peanuts (ground into paste, or smooth natural peanut butter)
2 tbsp tamarind paste (or substitute with 1½ tbsp rice vinegar + ½ tbsp lime juice)
½ tsp chili flakes (optional, for heat)

ingredients.title: For Garnish & Serving
items: Fresh cucumber slices or Thai cucumber relish (ajard)

instruction.title: Method
steps:
Step 1: Marinate the Chicken
• Slice chicken thighs into long strips (about 1.5 cm wide).
• Mix coconut milk, soy sauce, fish sauce, palm sugar, coriander, cumin, turmeric, curry powder, garlic, lemongrass, and vegetable oil in a bowl.
• Add chicken strips, coat well, cover, and marinate at least 4 hours (overnight preferred).

Step 2: Prepare the Peanut Sauce
• Heat a small saucepan over medium heat. Add a spoonful of coconut milk and the curry paste; sauté until fragrant (about 1 minute).
• Add the remaining coconut milk, ground peanuts, palm sugar, tamarind paste, fish sauce, and soy sauce.
• Simmer gently for 5–7 minutes until thickened. Adjust seasoning (balance of sweet, sour, salty, and nutty).
• Keep warm until serving.

Step 3: Grill the Satay
• Thread marinated chicken strips onto skewers (weave them for even cooking).
• Preheat grill or cast-iron griddle until very hot.
• Grill skewers for 2–3 minutes per side until lightly charred and cooked through (internal temp 74°C / 165°F).
• Brush lightly with coconut milk or marinade during grilling for extra juiciness.

Step 4: Plate & Serve
• Place 3–4 skewers per plate, slightly leaning over each other.
• Drizzle a little peanut sauce artistically on the side, serve the rest in a ramekin.
• Garnish with cucumber relish, lime wedge, cilantro sprig, and a sprinkle of crushed peanuts.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Pair with jasmine rice or sticky rice.
Serve extra peanut sauce on the side.
Enjoy with fresh lime wedges and toasted peanuts.

chefTips: Char is key: Aim for light caramelization without burning, which deepens flavor.
Balance flavors: Thai cooking is about harmony—taste the peanut sauce and adjust: add sugar if too sour, tamarind if too sweet, or fish sauce if flat.
Texture contrast: Always serve with something refreshing (ajard, cucumber relish) to cut through richness.
Presentation: Keep skewers neatly aligned, sauce cleanly plated, and garnish intentionally.
